newsitem.title: USA: Rayonier sees upward earnings trend.
newsitem.headline: Rayonier sees upward earnings trend.

text.p: Rayonier Inc, which earlier reported a loss after charges for the fourth quarter, said on Monday that it expects an upward earnings trend in the first quarter.

"Market conditions for both specialty pulp and timber and wood are stable and our costs are declining. With the two non-cash special charges behind us, we are better positioned to achieve the goals of increasing earnings growth and shareholder value over the long term," chairman and chief executive Ronald Gross said in a statement.
A Rayonier spokesman said the company has reported earnings per share of $0.52 in 1996's third quarter and $0.55 a share in the fourth quarter before charges.
The company posted charges of $2.63 a share for the planned closure of the Port Angeles Mill and $3.28 a share related to future environmental monitoring costs.

"In 1996, we had a strong first quarter, and after the industry pulp inventory correction we experienced in the second quarter, our earnings improved modestly in each of the last two quarters of the year," Gross said.
Rayonier reported earnings of $1.05 a share in last year's first quarter on sales of $294 million.
